solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clubs are controlled by cards opening to steward for entry

indicators.note: something controlled by another is held in its grip, so the first item sits inside the second
the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of steward is wanted

blocks.note: aces are high-value playing cards
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
the first letter of steward

explanation.surface: A doorman at a club checks membership cards before letting anyone in.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside ACES after the A, giving ACCES, and the S of steward completes ACCESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is the right or means of getting in, a straightforward synonym for admission.

clue.text: Barbarian one fired army up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the run is turned round

blocks.note: a means one, as in a single item
something fired has been lit
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A barbarian discharges his weapon at a whole army.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIT TA written upwards gives ATTILA.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun led the Huns, a people the Romans classed as barbarians, so he is an example of the type.

clue.text: Business in Treasury only half done (first in uncorks booze)

indicators.note: a job only half done stops midway, so the second half of Treasury is dropped
first in a word is its opening letter, so just the start of uncorks is used

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
taken as written
the first four of its eight letters
the first letter of uncorks

explanation.surface: Treasury work left half-finished while someone opens a bottle of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CO + IN + TREA + U spells COINTREAU; the bracketed part supplies both the last letter and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, so it is one particular kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Stoutish crook, hard to miss, doesn’t get involved

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order
to miss something is to leave it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rather portly villain, too unfit to join in, stays on the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H from STOUTISH to leave STOUTIS, then rearrange it as SITSOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out an activity is an idiom for declining to take part in it.

clue.text: In school, fun’s sadly out of order

indicators.note: in places one thing within another, so the shuffled letters go inside the school
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: a coed is a co-educational school, taking both boys and girls
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A school where pupils' enjoyment is gloomily out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: Coed, short for co-educational, is a mainly American word for a mixed school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something muddled has lost its proper sequence, so jumbled and disordered are synonymous senses here.

clue.text: Price’s dropped from demonstrated appliance

indicators.note: dropped from means taken out of the longer word, so those letters vanish

blocks.note: something demonstrated has been proven
pr. is a recognised abbreviation for price

explanation.surface: The cost of a kitchen gadget falls after a sales demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PR from PROVEN and OVEN is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is a kitchen device for baking and roasting, an example of a household appliance.

clue.text: Chiefs supporting Middle East country, alienated axis

indicators.note: to be alienated is to be pushed away, so that letter is sent off

blocks.note: someone supporting a cause is for it
Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula
y is the vertical axis of a graph

explanation.surface: Leaders backing a Middle Eastern state that has fallen out with its allies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axis' looks like a political alliance, but it is the Y axis of a graph, removed from YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremen are workers in charge of a crew, so they are bosses or heads of a team.

clue.text: Slithery creature, moving earth, finds rat

indicators.note: moving earth says the E letter for earth shifts to a new spot, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: a snake is a creature that slithers

explanation.surface: A snake burrowing through soil turns up a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Earth is E, and the E in SNAKE moves forward two places; 'rat' looks like the animal found, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform on them, which in British school slang is to sneak, a telltale's act.

clue.text: Summit in Denmark — ‘Is European island to be separate?’

indicators.note: the summit of a down word is its top letter, so only the start of Denmark is kept

blocks.note: the top letter of Denmark
taken as written
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: A Danish summit asks whether a European island should become independent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a political meeting, but it means the top letter of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means distinct and individually set apart, so it matches separate as an adjective.

clue.text: Tortuous match, West Indies overpowering English county finally

indicators.note: to overpower someone is to take their place by force, so one piece ousts another
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match
WI is the standard abbreviation for the West Indies
E is the abbreviation for English
the last letter of county

explanation.surface: A winding Test match in which the West Indies beat a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: WI replaces the E of TEST to give TWIST, then Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortuous describes something full of bends and turns, like a winding road.

clue.text: Unmatched? Don’t look so narrowly

definitions.note: a command split as two words, peer less

blocks.note: first meaning: without equal
second meaning: read as two words, an order to squint less

explanation.surface: Someone peering suspiciously at a supposedly unrivalled thing is told to stop squinting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into PEER LESS: to peer is to look narrowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means having no equal, so it is a direct synonym for unrivalled or incomparable.

clue.text: Heavy fire gets soldier in elbow

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the other word

blocks.note: to elbow your way through is to barge
RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner

explanation.surface: A soldier takes a hail of bullets and a blow to the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elbow' looks like the body part, but it is the verb meaning to push through roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a sustained artillery bombardment, an intense volley of gunfire.

clue.text: Beach strip enlightened tourist’s rear, it’s said

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: something enlightened has been lit up
the last letter of tourist
something spoken rather than written is oral

explanation.surface: A sunlit tourist's backside on a strip of beach, with a nod to gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it simply defines ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral as a noun names the coastal zone between high and low tide, the shoreline region.

clue.text: One going for a drag queen after kinky behaviour agreed

indicators.note: after says the royal piece follows the others rather than coming first

blocks.note: S&M, sadomasochism, is kinky sexual behaviour
OK means agreed
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: A drag queen, after some kinky business, says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag queen' reads as one phrase, but drag ends the definition and queen gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is a puff on a cigarette, so a person who takes one is a tobacco user.

clue.text: Fruit not all there

blocks.note: first meaning: yellow tropical fruits, in the plural
second meaning: crazy, mentally unbalanced

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a greengrocer's missing stock, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a yellow tropical fruit in plural, and is also slang for crazy or out of one's mind.

clue.text: Recreation, to doctor, meant Internet

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: For a GP, relaxing meant going online.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment is amusement or pleasant diversion, the same idea as leisure activity.

clue.text: Measuring instrument therefore used by Mike chopping tree

indicators.note: chopping breaks something up, so the letters of that word are mixed

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gauge, so to speak, used by a lumberjack named Mike felling a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ergometer is a device that records the work done by muscles, such as a rowing machine.

clue.text: Bill and Jack start to hire joiner, an expert

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: an ad, advertisement, is a bill
jack and AB, able seaman, both mean a sailor
the first letter of hire
and is a word that joins, a conjunction

explanation.surface: Two men set about hiring a carpenter who knows his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a woodworker, but it is the linking word AND; the clue's own 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a British idiom for someone highly skilled at a task.

clue.text: Retailer of Windows 2.0?

blocks.note: surface reading: a shop selling a computer operating system version
setter's reading: windows times two, the twin-paned kind sold door to door

explanation.surface: A computer shop selling an old version of Microsoft's operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: 2.0 reads as a software version, but it means two layers of glass in each window.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a seller markets windows with two panes of glass for insulation, a famously pushy British trade.

clue.text: Midday meal almost over at one (fruitcake)

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
over means covering, so the meal wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: lunch is the midday meal
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lunch is nearly finished at one o'clock, with fruitcake on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: LUNC wraps round AT I to give LUNATIC; 'fruitcake' looks like dessert but is slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruitcake in slang is an eccentric or crazy person, the same as a madman.

clue.text: Frozen thing that is outside church with baby

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the first piece wraps round the rest

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
CE is the Church of England
a cub is a baby animal such as a bear or fox

explanation.surface: Something frozen stands outside a church where a baby waits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cube is a small block of frozen water for chilling drinks.

clue.text: Aussie ignores advice with oxygen, regarding some peaks

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: Australia lies in the Antipodes, so an Australian is an Antipodean
a tip is a piece of advice
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An Australian climber shrugs off warnings and carries his own oxygen up the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TIP and O from ANTIPODEAN to leave ANDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means relating to the Andes, the long South American mountain range.

clue.text: Wine, as dry as this, spat out?

indicators.note: spat out means uttered, so the word is judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: the saying is as dry as a bone

explanation.surface: A wine taster finds a vintage so dry they spit it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat out' fits a wine tasting, where wine is spat, but here it means said.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a town in Burgundy that gives its name to the red and white wines made around it.

clue.text: Street fighter switched, becoming such a celeb?

definitions.note: an adjective-like label describing the celebrity's ranking

indicators.note: switched means the two parts swap places, so the second comes first

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali was a world champion boxer
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A street brawler changes sides and turns into a famous star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street fighter' reads as one phrase, but it is ST then ALI, which swap order.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of famous people, so a star celebrity belongs on it.

clue.text: See 18
My electronic hub

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
e- is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its central part, so a hub is a near synonym for the centre.

clue.text: A way into resorts?

indicators.note: read as re-sorts, it means the letters are sorted again into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
via is Latin for way or road
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about how holidaymakers get to their seaside destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: flying is how many people reach holiday resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation, air travel, is the usual route by which tourists reach distant holiday destinations.

clue.text: Creature, retracing furrow, stalled regularly

indicators.note: retracing your steps means going back the way you came
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a rut is a furrow or groove
the second, fourth and sixth letters of stalled

explanation.surface: An animal plodding back along a groove stops every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: RUT turned back gives TUR, then TLE completes TURTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a shelled reptile, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Type of residence converted — Edward was poorly

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
someone who was poorly ached

explanation.surface: A house is converted while its owner Edward is ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suits a house renovation, but it rearranges TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A detached house stands alone, not joined to any neighbour, a category of home in British estate-agent terms.

clue.text: Article published — ‘Hospital transferred capital’

indicators.note: a transferred hospital has moved site, so the H letter for hospital shifts place within its word

blocks.note: the is the definite article
a newspaper that ran a story published it

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reports that a hospital has moved to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Hospital is H, the letter in the article that moves one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the seat of government of Iran, so it is an example of a national capital city.
